newsitem.title: POLAND: Zloty flat vs basket, may inch higher on Tuesday.
newsitem.headline: Zloty flat vs basket, may inch higher on Tuesday.

text.p: The Polish zloty closed virtually flat at Friday's level against the basket of currencies after drifting mainly sideways during the day.

"Activity was light today and the zloty drifted around 3.06 percent from parity for most of the session, with the stable dollar/mark rate doing little to stir up trade," said Tomasz Nowakowski, forex dealer at Bank Handlowy SA.

Dealers said the zloty may get a slight boost on Tuesday as foreigners bought an estimated $40 million worth of bills at Monday's auction, but they said the zloty was not likely to rise past key resistance at 3.2 percent from parity tomorrow.
The zloty closed at 3.09/3.06 percent from the trading band centre, flat from Friday's 3.10/3.05 percent.
It closed at 3.1198/08 to the dollar, up from 3.1200/15 on Friday and at 1.8110/15 to the mark, flat from 1.8110/18.
Dealers said the central bank may intervene if the zloty strengthens past the 3.2 percent the resistance level.
But some said the central bank could refrain from currency buying on Tuesday to keep the Polish unit relatively strong and discourage speculative foreign capital flows.
On Wednesday the treasury will hold an extra mid-week 400 million zloty T-bill tender, it said after Monday's auction.

At today's T-bill tender the minimum price of the benchmark 52-week T-bill was flat at 81.85 and the treasury sold a total of 1.09 billion zlotys worth of bills after investors bid for 1.71 billion at the 1.1 billion tender.
The minimum price of the 26-week paper inched up 0.01 point to 90.03 while the minimum price of the 13-week paper inched down by the same amount to 94.75.
Overnight rates closed relatively flat 22.70/22.85 percent and tomorrow/next were at 22.75/22.95 vs Friday's 22.55/22.75.
